problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)={e}^{y}\,i+{e}^{x}\,j$ and $C$ is the line segment traversed from the point $A(2,0)$ to the point $B(4,2).$
worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the line segment.
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are 
$a=2\,i$ and $b=4\,i+2\,j.$
So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =(2\,i)+t[(4\,i+2\,j)-(2\,i)] \\  & =(2\,i)+t(2\,i+2\,j) \\  & =(2t+2)\,i+2t\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t=1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=2t+2\,y=2t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & ={e}^{y}\,i+{e}^{x}\,j \\  & ={e}^{2t}\,i+{e}^{2t+2}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t+2)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)j \\  & =2\,i+2\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =({e}^{2t}\,i+{e}^{2t+2}\,j)\cdot (2\,i+2\,j) \\  & ={e}^{2t}\cdot 2+{e}^{2t+2}\cdot 2 \\  & =2{e}^{2t}(1+{e}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2{e}^{2t}(1+{e}^{2})\,dt \\  & =(1+{e}^{2}){e}^{2t}{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(1+{e}^{2})({e}^{2}-1) \\  & ={e}^{4}-1\end{aligned}
$$
